findings.evidence: "the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month" versus "The finance liaison publishes the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year"
findings.fix: State a single owner and a single update cadence for the equipment catalog, and remove or reconcile the conflicting statement.
findings.location: Program Overview section, comparing paragraph 2 to the Special Cases section
findings.violation: The document names two different owners and two different update schedules for what appears to be the same equipment catalog, without reconciling the conflict.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team reviews the equipment catalog at the start of the fiscal year."
findings.fix: Consolidate all equipment catalog ownership and update information into one place in the document, naming a single responsible party and a single cadence.
findings.location: Questions and Updates section, final paragraph
findings.violation: This adds a third party and a third description of equipment catalog handling, on top of the IT asset group (monthly, in Program Overview) and finance liaison (fiscal year, in Special Cases) versions elsewhere in the document, so the reader cannot tell who actually owns the catalog.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person to match the rest of the document, for example "Employees must keep their equipment in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence switches to second person voice, "you" and "we", while every other section of the policy is written in third person, "Employees", "The manager", breaking the document's point of view without explanation.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Convert the sentences to third person to match the rest of the document, and add an actual definition of "stipend item" since this section's heading promises one.
findings.violation: This section also switches to second person voice, inconsistent with the third person voice used everywhere else in the policy, and despite the heading "Terminology Notes" it never actually defines what a "stipend item" is.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Merge this content into the How to Apply section as a single ordered list that matches the steps already described there, or explain explicitly how these steps relate to the portal process.
findings.violation: This one sentence process does not match the multi step process already described in the How to Apply section, starting a request in the portal, then reviewing a confirmation summary, then submitting, and it is unclear whether confirming eligibility and uploading a receipt are additional steps, a separate process, or a restatement of the same steps under different names.

findings.evidence: "The manager reviews the request within two business days" in Approval Timeline, "The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department" in Program Coordination, "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out" in Review Responsibility
findings.fix: Combine these three sections into a single Approval and Review section that lays out the full workflow in order, in one place.
findings.location: Approval Timeline, Program Coordination, and Review Responsibility sections
findings.violation: The approval and review workflow is described across three separate, non adjacent sections with no cross references between them, forcing the reader to assemble the full approval process from scattered fragments.

findings.evidence: "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year" versus "the policy applies to one device per category per employee"
findings.fix: Define "claim", "device", and "category", and state explicitly whether the one claim per year limit and the one device per category limit are the same restriction or apply together.
findings.location: Eligibility section, compared with Restrictions and Exceptions section
findings.violation: It is unclear whether these are two descriptions of the same limit or two independent limits, since neither "claim" nor "device" nor "category" is defined anywhere in the document, leaving the actual per employee cap ambiguous.

findings.evidence: "However, employees on an approved leave of absence remain eligible once they return to active status."
findings.fix: Replace "However" with a neutral connector such as "Separately", or remove it, and reserve "However" for places where an actual contrast exists.
findings.violation: "However" signals a contrast with the preceding sentence, but the prior sentence states the one claim per benefit year limit, which is not contradicted by leave of absence eligibility, so the transition misrepresents the logical relationship between the two ideas.

findings.evidence: "A copy of each update goes to the shared benefits folder the same day." appears word for word in both paragraphs of this section
findings.fix: State the shared folder rule once, at the section level, instead of repeating the same sentence for each update.
findings.violation: The identical sentence is repeated verbatim for two different updates, the reimbursement log and the equipment catalog, reading as duplicated filler rather than a confirmed shared rule.
